description: Reviewer-curated cross-reference relationships extracted from notwithstanding / does_not_apply / except_as_provided / supersedes phrasing in the Charlottetown bylaws. Loaded into zoning.structured_fact with fact_family='cross_references'. Out of 46 candidate clauses containing 'notwithstanding' alone, only the subset below carries a graph-actionable target reference; the rest are global standalone rules, within-clause back-references, or per-zone accessory-use templates and are intentionally not promoted to facts. See scripts/extract-charlottetown-override-candidates.py for the discovery/classification pipeline.

ignored_patterns.global_standalone: Clauses introduced by 'Notwithstanding any other provision/section/requirement of this by-law, ...' are standalone rules expressed with a notwithstanding phrase. They do not encode a graph edge to another section or zone; they are captured as `requirements` rows by the bylaw importer. Examples: doc-general-provisions-clause-4-4-1 (fences in yards), 5-17-1 (residential 45 m from sewage lagoon), 5-18-1/2 (cannabis retail 300 m / 1000 m buffers).
ignored_patterns.local_foregoing: Clauses with 'notwithstanding the foregoing' refer to the immediately preceding clause within the same section. They are within-clause qualifiers, not graph edges. Examples: doc-general-provisions-clause-5-9-1-g (commercial vehicle), 6-10-2 (building setback exception).
ignored_patterns.accessory_use_template: 13 zone clauses in the current bylaw use the identical phrase 'Notwithstanding the requirements, the following are permitted as accessory or secondary uses:' to introduce per-zone accessory-use lists. These are already captured as `uses` rows with use_status='accessory_or_secondary'; promoting them to relationship facts would duplicate.
ignored_patterns.except_as_provided_global: Most 'except as otherwise permitted in this bylaw' phrasing acknowledges the existence of carve-outs without naming a specific target. Treated as phrasing convention rather than a graph edge. Re-evaluate if an entry names a specific section.
ignored_patterns.self_excluding_section: Clauses such as 'This section shall not apply to lots ... created prior to the effective date of this by-law' (48-1-2 / 7-1-2) self-limit the section in which they appear. They are temporal/applicability conditions, not cross-references.
